$comment: Which published bundle-manifest schema version each DCC host's consumer has been VERIFIED
against — not merely which it tolerates. The canonical schema is published at
https://mantle.place/.well-known/schemas/bundle-manifest/ — vN.json for the integer
pre-history, X.Y.Z.json (no v prefix, e.g. 1.0.0.json) for the MPB semver era — and is
never copied here.
Raising a pin is a claim that the host's parser was exercised against that shape and its
tests updated. check_manifest_conformance.py fails when the platform publishes newer.
Add an entry when a new host lands (revit, rhino, blender, max). One contract, N consumers.
A host registers here from its FIRST commit (HPS-38).
OWNERSHIP IS PER KEY. Each host key belongs to that host's maintainers: a Revit change edits
`revit` and nothing else, and never needs to coordinate with an Unreal change to bump its own
pin. This file's SCHEMA — the shape of a host entry, the $comment, and
check_manifest_conformance.py itself — is maintainer-owned; propose changes by pull
request. Adding or removing a host key is a schema-level change; changing the numbers inside
your own key is not.
Required fields per host, all consumed by the gate:
verifiedAgainstManifestVersion — the version the parser was exercised against: a JSON
int for the integer pre-history (19), a semver STRING
for the MPB era ("1.0.0"). The JSON type is what tells
the two families apart.
verifiedAgainstCorpusVersion   -- int; the corpus/index.json top-level corpusVersion this
host's suite was last reviewed against. corpusVersion bumps
on a breaking change to the corpus's own case-field shape
(not on adding cases). The gate fails when this trails the
corpus's actual corpusVersion, same shape as the manifest
version check -- a host that hasn't reviewed a corpus-shape
change is exactly the drift this field exists to catch.
evidence                       — prose; WHAT was exercised. Refreshed on every bump.
consumer                       — repo-relative path to the parser itself.
floorSource                    — {path, pattern}: where this host's clean-break version
floor is declared, and a regex whose FIRST capture group
is the version — an integer-era number (18) or a semver
string ("1.0.0"). Host-language-agnostic on purpose —
a C++ header, a C# const and a Python module are all a
file and a regex (HPS-39).
tests                          — repo-relative path named in the remediation message when
web publishes newer than this pin.
owner                          — who owns this key; maintainer-owned.
groups                         -- the corpus groups this host's suite claims (HPS-41).
Machine-readable so the gate can DERIVE per-case host
coverage (groups x appliesTo) and ratchet it against
coverage-baseline.json instead of trusting the
evidence prose. Claiming a group is a promise to run
every case in it.

unreal.evidence: MantlePlaceImportManifestTest.cpp drives the shared conformance corpus' `manifest` group (HPS-40): it reads corpus/index.json at run time, so every accept/reject vector and every derived expectation — placement math, EPSG, the v18 per-host dcc_readiness normalization, the retired v17 anonymous mesh_import asserted IGNORED, and every pre-v19 version rejected by the clean-break gate — lives in one language-neutral artifact rather than in C++ literals. A case edited to expect something different turns this suite red. The reader implements asserted-keys semantics (HPS-46, ported from the Revit reader): every expectations key of an executed case must be READ by a typed assertion, so an unknown key, a known key declared with the wrong JSON type, and an assertion path that never ran all fail identically; the reader also runs the corpus/self-test/ fixtures and fails if any is accepted. The materialization verdict follows the neutral signals (HPS-47) — a bundle materialized for another host parses as materialized, not as base. The corpus accept shape is the platform's published v19 schema and its reference fixture. Repinned to v19 on 2026-08-10: the two things v19 changed for THIS host are pinned rather than assumed. manifest.deliveryReasonNotProduced drives `not_produced`/`not_selected` — values that did not exist through v18, since closing `reason` into #/$defs/deliveryReason required growing the set — through the reader and asserts the reason is surfaced verbatim (HPS-36) rather than matched on. manifest.revitBlockIgnored carries an `unreal.georeference` in metric UTM beside a conflicting `revit.georeference` in a State Plane foot zone, so a reader that keyed placement off whichever block it found first would report the wrong EPSG and fail (HPS-33); the materialization vector's revit row now carries a v19-declared sub-object instead of the `landxml` guess v19 explicitly did not include. Not exercised, and deliberately not claimed: nothing in the `revit` block beyond its presence — that is revit's own pin to raise. The v19 `unreal.landscape_layers` block is CONSUMED rather than skipped: manifest.full carries all eight sub-blocks with their `ue_ready` companions and the suite asserts every leaf - path, sha256, encoding, width/height, size_bytes and the `value_mapping` shape each `encoding` dictates (RGBA bands, mask true/false, indexed class codes, the 16-bit min/max ramp with its to_value formula and optional units/nodata, the 8-bit identity passthrough) - so a companion the pipeline adds cannot ride in unread. materialWeightBands pins the one derivation the band legend exists for, `materials[]` resolved to (companion, RGBA channel); it is host-neutral, which is why it is a corpus expectation and not a local assertion, while the resample onto a Landscape post grid stays host-local. The companions are declared 143x142 against a 1009-post heightmap on purpose: the weight rasters ride the DEM's own grid, so a consumer assuming they match the Landscape resolution is wrong. `up_axis` on `mesh_alternative` and `buildings_mesh` is now fail-closed on anything but "y" (the axis Interchange's unconditional Y-up conversion assumes), the way planet_shape has always been. Five sibling suites consume the vault, auth, cache, digest and projection groups the same way; the vault error-body parser follows the HPS-48 precedence. The floor constant deliberately stays at 18 while this pin is 19: the readers gate `<`, so v19 is accepted and now exercised, but the clean-break floor is NOT this host's to move alone. The shared corpus is written against ONE floor — cache/validity-truth-table.json's rows are absolute (manifestVersion 18 must read VALID for a host floored at 18 and ManifestTooOld for one floored at 19, and no single fixture is both) and the pre-floor reject set is host-invariant. Floors move in lockstep when the last host takes the break; pins move per host, on evidence. It is cross-checked against corpus/index.json's manifestVersion as `floor <= corpus`. The placement expectations were re-derived on 2026-08-18 when this host's world-axis convention was corrected from East->+X to North->+X: Unreal's world is left-handed, so mapping the projected frame's easting onto +X swapped two axes of a Z-up frame, which is a reflection rather than a rotation and mirrored every import across the NE diagonal (visible as a 90-degree rotation on a near-square AOI, and as buildings needing a -1 Y scale to sit on their own terrain). No manifest field changed and no value was recomputed - landscapeScale, landscapeSpawnLocation and drapeWorldRect* are the same numbers with their X and Y components exchanged, which is exactly what a pure axis-order fix should look like in a diff. REPINNED to MPB 1.0.0 (2026-08-22), and this is the first repin that also MOVED THE FLOOR: the earlier evidence recorded that the floor deliberately stayed at 18 while the pin was 19, because the shared corpus is written against ONE floor and the pre-floor reject set is host-invariant, so floors move in lockstep when the last host takes the break. Both registered hosts take it here, together, which is what let the reject ladder finally close the integer era by adding v18 and v19. The floor is now a semver STRING, and the gate enforces a rule that ordering alone does not: a host pinned in the semver era may not leave an integer floor behind, because a reader gating numerically reads a semver version as 0 and refuses every manifest it claims to support. What is exercised at 1.0.0: the whole corpus `manifest` group in its key-mapped shape (hosts.<hostId> with readiness folded in, snake_case throughout, the legacy terrain/runtime/dcc_readiness blocks retired); the version gate in BOTH directions, which the integer era could not express — an unknown higher MAJOR is refused gracefully with a distinct remedy (update the plugin) from the too-old refusal (re-download the AOI), while a higher MINOR is accepted because minors are strictly additive; and the near-misses that are how a reader drifts into dual-parsing — an integer-as-string "19", a partial "1.0", a pre-release tag "1.0.0-rc1", and a leading-zero "01.0.0" that semver forbids — pinned as the shared corpus reject cases manifest.reject.versionIntegerString / versionPartial / versionPrerelease / versionLeadingZero, which this corpus-driven suite refuses through the same clean-break gate. This tree carries no Unreal-local near-miss test; the corpus cases are the binding assertion, and the leading-zero acceptance itself was found and fixed by the Revit host's test — a defect the Unreal parser shared. Materialization is now decided from ONE neutral signal rather than three: everything host-specific lives under `hosts`, so the predicate asks whether that object has any key and never which, and an empty `hosts` is scaffolding exactly as an empty `vector.layers` is. The cache truth table deliberately spans the era break — its at-the-floor rows are "1.0.0" and its too-old rows are 19, the pre-history's top being the neighbour immediately below a semver floor in the total order, which is the row a host comparing only within one family gets wrong. NOT COMPILED BY CI: this repository does not build the Unreal plugin (that runs on private infrastructure), so the C++ half of this repin is verified by review and by this gate's floor read, not by a compiler or a test run. That lag is published in README.md and is the reason this entry says what was changed rather than what was observed passing.

revit.evidence: ManifestConformanceTests.cs drives the shared conformance corpus' `manifest` group (HPS-40): it reads corpus/index.json at run time and dispatches every case that is not scoped to another host, so the 12 host-invariant cases and this host's own three v19 cases bind this parser — the seven pre-v18 version rejects and the unversioned/malformed pair (clean break, HPS-31), the base-on-demand partial parse that must still yield orderId, layout.cesiumTerrain and packaging.delivery_model before refusing (HPS-37), the two top-level `vector` road-spline selection cases (name AND format, no fallback to a format this host cannot read), and the materialization-signals table (HPS-47) driven through CheckMaterialized. The twelve `appliesTo: "unreal"` cases are skipped by construction (HPS-41); the three `appliesTo: "revit"` ones are this host's own. manifest.revitArtifactHashes drives a v19 shape carrying all three deliverable sub-objects and asserts each artifact surfaces ITS OWN sha256 — v19 publishes those hashes in the `revit` block and NOWHERE else, so a reader still taking them off the v18 `elevation.points_csv` and `buildings.ifc` detail blocks surfaces three unverifiable artifacts with every other assertion still green, which was the hole this case closes. manifest.revitOwnGeoreference is new with this change and drives the survey point. Through v19 this host resolved it from `delivery.local_origin` ALONE, which the ETL emits on the `local_ft` tier alone, so a metric-tier bundle produced SkipReasonCode.NoSurveyPoint and the model was imported not georeferenced at all — while the origin sat in the manifest addressed to this host by name. The case states three origins in conflict on purpose (`unreal.georeference.origin.utm`, `delivery.local_origin`, and `revit.georeference.origin.projected` in a State Plane foot zone) and pins the resolved easting, northing, EPSG, linear unit and grid rotation, so a reader that merges them or takes whichever it finds first reports 32613 and fails while every other assertion stays green. It is the mirror of manifest.revitBlockIgnored, which points the same trap at the reference host. Three things it binds that the earlier revit cases did not: the own block is PRIMARY and `delivery.local_origin` the FALLBACK, so the `local_ft` bundles already in curators' hands keep working without a coordinated pipeline release; `origin.projected.linear_unit` travels WITH the coordinates rather than being assumed metric, because it is the ORIGIN's unit and differs from each artifact's own `units` on the foot tiers, where reading it as metres places the site 3.28x out; and `grid_rotation_deg` is deliberately non-zero in the fixture, since the emitters reproject per-vertex and publish 0.0 today, so a fixture that agreed would be passed by the hardcoded zero the shim used to send to ProjectPosition. The elevation half of that hardcode is now SurveyPointPlacement.ElevationM in the pure core, zero for the reason the block's own units_note states rather than by coincidence. manifest.reject.revitHashMissing drives a present `surface_dxf` sub-object with no `sha256` and requires the refusal to name it: that is the Revit half of HPS-34, which bound nothing for this host until v19 gave it artifacts whose hashes the schema makes required-when-present. The version gate on that rule is exercised host-locally in ManifestReaderTests.cs, because no shared fixture can be both: a v18 bundle publishing no Revit hashes at all still parses and reports its artifacts valid-but-unverified rather than corrupt, which is the case the required-when-present reading exists to protect. The hash is read off this host's OWN block (HPS-33), and a sub-object naming a DIFFERENT file than the resolved layout pointer has its hash discarded rather than transplanted — checking one file's bytes against another file's hash reports a corruption that is not there. Repinned to v19 on 2026-08-10, on this host's own evidence rather than in lockstep with the reference. Four reader behaviours were proven by making them fail on purpose: a working tree with no reachable corpus fails the suite rather than skipping it; a claimed group that resolves to zero cases fails; a case naming a missing vector file fails; and an unrecognised `expectations` key fails. The reader's asserted-keys semantics — recording which keys were actually READ, so a case declaring a key it does recognise but with the wrong JSON type (`"orderId": 999`) fails instead of asserting nothing while still counting as covered — became the normative rule for every host (HPS-46), and the reader also runs the corpus/self-test/ fixtures and fails if any is accepted. The floor constant deliberately stays at 18 while this pin is 19: the reader gates `<`, so v19 is accepted and now exercised, but the clean break is not this host's to take alone — the shared corpus is written against ONE floor (cache/validity-truth-table.json's rows are absolute), so floors move in lockstep while pins move per host. It is cross-checked against corpus/index.json's manifestVersion as `floor <= corpus` in the same run. AuthConformanceTests.cs drives the `auth` group's four vector cases: the RFC 7636 Appendix B S256 pair and the base64url triples (HPS-04), the callback parse table and the state-validation rows including the empty-expected-state row that is the whole of HPS-07, the grant-response table with the expires_in<=0 substitution and the refresh-token preservation rule (HPS-10), the HPS-48 error precedence asserted by removing one field at a time rather than only reading the first, and the five-state machine evaluated over every one of the 45 (state x event) pairs rather than only the 13 rows the table spells out -- the unmatched remainder is where the unchanged-by-default rule lives. All four are `expect: "vector"` and so carry no `expectations` keys for HPS-46's asserted-keys check to bind, so VectorDocument applies the same idea one level down: every leaf value in every vector file must be READ by a typed assertion or the case fails with the path, which is what stops a suite driving row 0 of an eleven-row table and reporting the case as covered. That stricter reading is this host's own until the proposed HPS-46 amendment lands, and it is proven by VectorDocumentSelfTests making it fail on purpose. The expiry skew is a constant with no parameter, so the reference host's skew defect (a shim passing SkewSeconds=0) is unrepresentable here rather than merely absent. VaultConformanceTests.cs drives the `vault` group's fourteen cases, each a different entry point, so this group carries the UndrivenCases check the single-loop manifest suite cannot use: the HPS-20 unknown-is-not-zero listing (every optional integrity fact nullable, and the legacy row's nulls asserted as hasX=false rather than as values), the HPS-21 split between a skipped malformed ROW and a response that is not a listing at all, the HPS-22 status and materialize-state synonym buckets with case-insensitivity and unknown-is-never-an-error both asserted behaviourally, the HPS-23 explicit token list (this host sends its own seven Revit tokens and never a host-name keyword — widened from five for the `vector.geojson` and `landcover.tree_points_csv` layers the Forma-parity steps consume, and still an explicit client-owned list rather than a scope keyword — with the corpus's scope vectors substituted per the vector's own instruction), the HPS-24 single-flight join recognised by BODY SHAPE, the HPS-25 status table including absent-progress-is-indeterminate and a failed job parsing SUCCESSFULLY with its reason surfaced, and the HPS-48 error precedence walked one key at a time so an implementation cannot pass by reading whichever field happens to be first. One precedence implementation serves both auth and vault, which is the fix. CacheConformanceTests.cs drives `cache` and `digest`: the eleven-row HPS-27 truth table with every step of the declared precedence asserted to be REACHED by some row, the HPS-30 sanitisation vectors with the suffix recomputed over the RAW id, and the FIPS 180-4 known answers plus streaming equivalence across a block boundary. One thing is deliberately NOT asserted and is recorded rather than quietly skipped: nested `expectations` keys generally, which HPS-46 does not reach. The second, `items[].tierLabel`, is no longer a deviation: it was one host's answer riding a host-invariant case, and now has its own `appliesTo: "unreal"` case that this suite skips as a unit. Host-local coverage beyond the corpus: the v18 delivery-block enums fail closed on an unrecognised value (HPS-35), the import planner's topo-path precedence and pointer resolution, and the points-file reader. On the client side: the HPS-16 null store is exercised on the Linux runner where DPAPI does not exist, and the DPAPI store's plaintext-never-on-disk, decrypt-failure-is-absence (HPS-17) and HPS-30-sanitised storage keys are exercised on Windows; the bundle cache is keyed by order id through the HPS-30 sanitiser, and the retained/transient extraction split is asserted rather than reviewed. The promote-by-rename path of HPS-26 is exercised end to end — a verified download is renamed and its sidecar written, a hash or size mismatch deletes the .part and never creates bundle.zip, a cancellation deletes the .part and fires no completion, and a .part left by a killed process is discarded rather than resumed. The `projection` group IS claimed as of the Forma-parity work, and the claim is narrow enough to state exactly. Until the Forma-parity work it was deliberately unclaimed and said so here, because every placement value this host consumed arrived pre-derived: it applied the manifest's survey point verbatim through ProjectLocation.SetProjectPosition and computed no easting, northing or zone of its own (HPS-33). The road-centreline and site-boundary steps change that and nothing else. Their source layers are `vector` GeoJSON, and RFC 7946 fixes those at WGS84 lon/lat, so the manifest describes the LAYER while every vertex inside it is still geographic — the one narrow case HPS-45 permits a host to project for, and the only projection this host performs. ProjectionConformanceTests.cs drives projection.lonLatToUtm through GeoProjection.TryLonLatToUtm: the known-answer pair to the table's own 0.05 m tolerance, the southern-hemisphere row asserted through the 10 000 km false northing rather than through a round trip, and both reject rows (a non-UTM EPSG, and a latitude outside the validity band) as refusals rather than best efforts. Being an `expect: "vector"` case it carries no `expectations` keys, so VectorDocument's leaf tracker binds it the way it binds `auth` — the table's `source` and `toleranceMetres` are read, not skimmed. The tree-points layer is NOT part of the claim: it ships absolute AOI-UTM, so it is placed by subtracting the same published origin and projects nothing. What the two share is the refusal. Where the bundle's origin is in a CRS this host can neither project into nor subtract within — a State Plane foot tier, whose origin is EPSG:2231 while the tree points stay UTM and the GeoJSON stays lon/lat — the layer is skipped with SkipReasonCode.CoordinateSystemNotSupported rather than placed ~2000 km away, and that decision sits in the pure core where ImportPlannerTests asserts it. The imagery drape lands with the Forma-parity work and the parser now reads three more host-neutral blocks for it: `layout.imagery_drape` as the pointer of record (HPS-32), `imagery.gsd_m` and `imagery.present`, and `elevation.dem.bounds_target_crs`/`crs` as the drape's ground extent. That last one is READ BUT NOT DECLARED — the published v19 schema gives `elevation.dem` only `units`, `horizontal_units` and `zones` under additionalProperties, while the extent that IS declared sits in `unreal.imagery_drape`, which this host may not read (HPS-36). So the pin covers a field the schema does not describe, and the planner does not trust it on the manifest's word: it is used only when the drape PNG's own IHDR grid times `imagery.gsd_m` reproduces the extent within 2 px, and otherwise the drape is skipped with SkipReasonCode.ExtentNotCorroborated. A host-neutral `imagery.drape` block is proposed to the platform and is preferred wherever a bundle publishes one; when it lands, the DEM fallback and the corroboration are both deletable. No corpus case was proposed for any of this on purpose — a shared case built on an undeclared field would bind every host to the coincidence this host refuses to rely on. Observed passing on hosted runners at the repin: dotnet build clean and every suite green on .NET 8 (Revit 2025/2026) and .NET 10 (Revit 2027) — 22/22 manifest conformance, 34/34 import planner, 12/12 bundle cache. Two defects were found by tests rather than review and are fixed: a sidecar that wrote the version unquoted once it became a string, producing JSON that failed to parse back; and the leading-zero acceptance above, which the Unreal parser shared. RevitArtifactHashVersion is DELETED rather than ported — it gated the hash requirement at v19 because the floor still accepted v18, which published no Revit hashes, and every version the 1.0.0 floor accepts publishes them, so the branch could never be taken and read as a live rule protecting a case that no longer exists.
